questions.q: How does the summary explain why exercise helps the brain work better?
a: It improves blood flow and spurs new cell growth
It reduces the brain's need for nutrients
It slows the heart so the mind can rest
It replaces sleep for most people
questions.why: Lesson 1 says exercise improves circulation, helps form new blood vessels and stimulates hormones including BDNF.

questions.q: What role does BDNF play, according to the summary?
a: It supports new cell creation and healthy neurons
It carries oxygen directly to the lungs
It signals the body when to sleep
It blocks the formation of new blood vessels
questions.why: Lesson 1 identifies brain-derived neurotrophic factor as a hormone that helps create new cells and keeps neural connections healthy.

questions.q: What does the summary say happens if you sleep six hours or less for five nights?
a: You are as impaired as after two days without sleep
You adapt and perform better than usual
You need only a short nap to recover fully
Your sleep cycle permanently changes type
questions.why: Lesson 2 compares five nights of six hours or less to going 48 hours straight without sleep in terms of cognitive impairment.

questions.q: According to the summary, what are people called who naturally wake early?
a: Larks
Owls
Hummingbirds
Doves
questions.why: Lesson 2 says early risers are larks, late sleepers are night owls, and most people shift between the two like hummingbirds.

questions.q: What did Richard Mayer's experiment find about how people learn best?
a: Those who both saw and heard the material remembered most
Those who only heard it outperformed everyone
Those who only saw it recalled the most detail
All three groups performed about the same
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the group that received information through both sight and sound performed far better when tested on what they had seen.
